why: I checked each verifier check's PASS/FAIL conditions against the words of its expect line. Check 1's sample values ("00042", "   42", "**ab", "xxx") all follow from left padding with fill, using a space as the default, up to width. Check 2 only tests cases where s is width characters or longer and expects s back unchanged. Check 3 fails only when an exported function has no README heading. "Section" fairly implies a heading, and "with section text below it" is a mild gloss of the same idea, not a separate test. Check 4 needs exit code 0 and "# fail 0". With node --test that is the same thing as passing, not an extra rule. The stricter items, test coverage for padLeft, README accuracy and multi-character fill, sit under "Advisory (not part of any PASS/FAIL)". No mutation, branch or file-scope rule appears in any condition.
